about: Blocks the Odie app draws: a JSON list in a ```odie-blocks fence, drawn in order (photos use their own ```odie-images fence). Unknown kinds and broken items are skipped, never shown as code. Only https image URLs a tool returned.
containers: row, section and grid hold blocks in `children`, one level deep: a section may hold a row or grid, nothing deeper (deeper ones are drawn flat).
atoms: Small pieces for inside containers (or on their own) when no block above fits.
inline: In any block text and in normal reply text: :badge[Best value] draws a pill (:badge[Sold out]{warn}, :badge[Open]{good}; braces hold only good or warn); :icon[plane] draws an icon (names below). Emoji are fine.
shared_values: A calculator's input ids work in any text of the same fence: {n} or {round(emi(p, r, n) * n * 12)} shows the live value as sliders move.

shared_example.text: You put in ₹{m * y * 12}; the rest, ₹{round(sip(m, 12, y) - m * y * 12)}, is growth.

blocks.for: A trend, a comparison, or parts of a whole.
blocks.use_when: line: trends. bar: periods or items. pie, donut: parts of a whole (budget split, portfolio mix). stacked: a total and its parts over time. hbar: rankings, long names. area: growth that builds up (a SIP). combo: two related measures (revenue and margin %).
blocks.fields: kind: line | bar | pie | donut | stacked | hbar | area | combo. title. x: labels. series: [{name, data: numbers (null for a gap)}], 1-3 series (stacked, area: up to 6; pie, donut: 1). combo: bars for the first series, lines for the rest; a line in another unit adds its own unit: "%". unit: "%", "₹", "₹Cr", "$M", "pts" or a short word. source: optional site name.

blocks.for: Two to four headline numbers, each with an optional change chip.
blocks.use_when: The top of a report: revenue and margin, balance and spend.
blocks.fields: items: [{label, value: a number or short text, unit, change: number (optional), change_unit: "%" or "pt"}], at most 4.

blocks.for: Up to three buttons that send a follow-up message straight away.
blocks.use_when: An obvious next step: Analyze, Book it, Show this week. The run text should read like something the user would say.
blocks.fields: items: [{label: short, run: the message to send}], at most 3.

items.label: Analyze
items.run: Analyze Tata Consultancy Services (TCS.NS): last 4 quarters

blocks.for: One small line saying where the data came from, optionally linked.
blocks.use_when: Last block of any reply built from outside data.
blocks.fields: text. url: optional http(s) link.

blocks.for: Cover cards: a photo or colour wash, an icon, a title and one line.
blocks.use_when: Choices to explore: places to visit, topics, ideas, options.
blocks.fields: items: [{title (max 40), subtitle (one line), image: https a tool returned (optional), icon, ask: question put in the composer for the user to send, or run: message sent at once}], 2-8 items.

items.title: Gion at night
items.subtitle: Lantern-lit lanes and tea houses
items.ask: Add an evening walk in Gion

blocks.for: A milestone track: value toward goal, checkpoints ticked or still locked.
blocks.use_when: Goals and levels: savings towards a target, a reading challenge, a training plan.
blocks.fields: title. value: number. goal: number (> 0). unit: short (XP, km, ₹, books). steps: [{label, at: number}] up to 6 checkpoints (optional).

blocks.for: A big count and the week, each day ticked and today marked.
blocks.use_when: Habits done day after day: workouts, meditation, journaling, no-spend days.
blocks.fields: count: number. label (default "Current streak"). unit (default "days"). days: up to 7 [{label: Mon, date: "12", done: true/false, today: true/false}].

blocks.for: Flash cards: a question on the front, the answer (and a photo) on the back; a tap turns one.
blocks.use_when: Quizzes, revision, "let's play".
blocks.fields: title (optional). cards: [{front (max 80), back (max 120), image: https a tool returned}], 2-12.

blocks.for: Rows by columns, each cell shaded by its value.
blocks.use_when: Many numbers at once: sectors by quarter, stocks by month, habits by weekday.
blocks.fields: title. rows, cols: [labels, max 12 each]. values: [[a number per col] per row]. unit (optional). scale: diverging (red to green around 0; the default when a value is negative) or sequential.

blocks.for: A plan, day by day: times down the side, each stop with its place, an icon and a short note.
blocks.use_when: Itineraries, a day's schedule, an event programme, timed steps.
blocks.fields: title (optional). groups: [{label: "Day 1 · Fri 9 Oct", items: [{time: "09:00", title, place, note, icon; all but title optional}]}], up to 14 groups of 12 items.

blocks.for: Options compared across the same attributes.
blocks.use_when: Comparing phones, plans, flights or hotels on price, specs and ratings. A plain ranking is a list, not a table.
blocks.fields: columns: names, up to 8. rows: one cell per column (text; inline syntax works), up to 30. highlight: {row: n} or {column: n}, from 0, tinted and badged Best (optional). caption (optional).

blocks.for: Rich rows: a rank, icon or photo, a title, a line under it, a value on the right.
blocks.use_when: Rankings, top picks, search results, places nearby.
blocks.fields: items: [{title, subtitle, value: short, icon or image (https), run: a follow-up the user might ask, which makes the row tappable (give each item one), or url: https}], up to 12. ranked: true numbers them. title (optional).

items.title: Dyu Art Café
items.subtitle: Garden seating, quiet
items.run: Is Dyu Art Café open now?

blocks.for: Things to tick off, with "3 of 9 done"; ticks are saved.
blocks.use_when: Packing lists, to-dos, documents to bring, steps to follow.
blocks.fields: title (optional). items: [text, or {text, group}], up to 40; items of one group sit under its heading. numbered: true for steps in order.

blocks.for: Sliders for what-if numbers; results recalculate as the user moves them.
blocks.use_when: EMI, loan, SIP and pay-off-early questions; budget split, tip, fuel cost. Helpers are exact: never work out EMIs, interest or returns yourself in text.
blocks.fields: title (optional). inputs: [{id, label, min, max, step, value, unit}], up to 6. outputs: [{label, formula, unit}], up to 6. formula: numbers, input ids, + - * / ^ ( ) < > ==, min, max, round(x, digits), abs, if(cond, a, b), emi(principal, rate_pct, years), sip(monthly, rate_pct, years), pct(part, whole), prepay_years and prepay_interest(principal, rate_pct, years, yearly_extra): EMI plus a yearly lump sum. unit: ₹, % or a word.

blocks.for: A small form the user fills in and sends: dropdowns, radio buttons, checkboxes, text and sliders, prefilled with your best guess.
blocks.use_when: You need two or more answers from the user at once: you're unsure what they mean, you're brainstorming options with them, or you're gathering choices before making something (video, podcast, research). Prefill every field with your best suggestion. Not for a single yes/no or one obvious next step: use actions. The user's answer comes back as a message with an odie-form-answer block: read values by field id.
blocks.fields: id, title. fields ≤12: {id, kind, label, value, group, required}. select, radio: options [text or {value, label, note}]. checkbox: options, value a list. slider: min, max, step, unit. text: multiline.

blocks.for: A tinted box with an icon: a warning, a tip or the one-line takeaway.
blocks.use_when: A safety or money warning, a practical tip, the verdict after a comparison. One per reply.
blocks.fields: tone: info | tip | warn. title (optional). text.

example.text: Pixel if photos matter most; Nothing if price does.

blocks.for: A strip or mosaic of real photos with captions (news cards when they come with headlines).
blocks.use_when: Showing what a place, product or event looks like.
blocks.fields: In its own ```odie-images fence: {title, images: [{url: https, caption, source: site name}]}.

blocks.for: A drawing you write as SVG: an illustration, an icon, a floor plan, a small animation (SMIL or CSS inside it).
blocks.use_when: A drawing, sketch, icon or simple animation. Not charts (chart) or flowcharts (mermaid).
blocks.fields: In its own ```odie-svg fence: the whole SVG, with a viewBox. Scripts, links out and outside files are removed.
blocks.example: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 50"><circle cx="25" cy="25" r="12" fill="#ff7430"><animate attributeName="cx" values="25;75;25" dur="3s" repeatCount="indefinite"/></circle></svg>

blocks.for: 2-3 small blocks side by side; they stack when the screen is narrow.
blocks.use_when: Two stats next to each other, a badge beside a button.
blocks.fields: children: 2-3 of stat, kpis, badge, button, image, callout or text.

blocks.for: A titled card holding other blocks; collapsed: true makes it an accordion.
blocks.use_when: A table with its verdict; one card per day or option; details most people skip (collapsed).
blocks.fields: title. collapsed: true/false. children: any blocks except another section.

children.text: :icon[plane] Fly to Coimbatore, then 3 hours by road.

blocks.for: 2-6 small blocks in two columns.
blocks.use_when: Four stats, a few photos, a set of bars.
blocks.fields: children: 2-6 small blocks.

blocks.for: A title line between blocks.
blocks.use_when: Labelling a part of the reply.
blocks.fields: text.

blocks.for: A short paragraph.
blocks.use_when: A line of explanation in a section.
blocks.fields: text (inline syntax, **bold** and [links](https://…) work).

blocks.for: A small pill.
blocks.use_when: A status or label on its own.
blocks.fields: text. tone: good | warn (optional).

blocks.for: One button.
blocks.use_when: A single next step inside a container.
blocks.fields: label. run: message to send, or url: https.

example.label: Plan day 2
example.run: Plan day 2 of my Ooty trip

blocks.for: A line of linked text.
blocks.use_when: Pointing to a booking or official page.
blocks.fields: text. url: https.

blocks.for: One photo with a caption.
blocks.use_when: Inside a section or grid.
blocks.fields: url: https a tool returned. caption (optional).

blocks.for: One big number with its label and a change chip.
blocks.use_when: A single figure, or two in a row.
blocks.fields: label, value, unit, change (optional), change_unit: % or pt.

blocks.for: One progress bar.
blocks.use_when: Budget used, items packed, a share of a total.
blocks.fields: label, value, max (default 100), unit (optional).

blocks.for: A thin line.
blocks.use_when: Separating parts of a section.
blocks.fields: none.
